facts.text: The gull-billed tern has a short, thick gull-like bill, broad wings, long legs and a robust body that set it apart from most terns.
facts.quote: the short thick gull-like bill, broad wings, long legs and robust body are distinctive.

facts.text: In summer the adult shows grey upperparts, white underparts, a black cap and a strong black bill.
facts.quote: The summer adult has grey upperparts, white underparts, a black cap, strong black bill and black legs.

facts.text: In winter the black cap is lost and replaced by a dark patch through the eye.
facts.quote: In winter, the cap is lost, and there is a dark patch through the eye like a Forster's tern or a Mediterranean gull.

facts.text: It nests in colonies on lakes, marshes and coasts, laying two to five eggs in a ground scrape.
facts.quote: The gull-billed tern breeds in colonies on lakes, marshes and coasts (including bays and earthen levees). It nests in a ground scrape and lays two to five eggs.

facts.text: Unlike most terns, it does not normally plunge dive for fish and has a broader diet than most other terns.
facts.quote: It does not normally plunge dive for fish like the other white terns, and has a broader diet than most other terns.

facts.text: It largely feeds on insects caught in flight, and also hunts over wet fields for amphibians and small mammals.
facts.quote: It largely feeds on insects taken in flight, and also often hunts over wet fields and even in brushy areas, to take amphibians and small mammals.

facts.text: It is an opportunistic feeder and has been seen picking up dead dragonflies from roads.
facts.quote: It is also an opportunistic feeder, and has been observed to pick up and feed on dead dragonflies from the road.

facts.text: The species breeds across southern Europe, Asia, both coasts of North America and eastern South America.
facts.quote: It breeds in warmer parts of the world in southern Europe, temperate and eastern Asia, both coasts of North America, eastern South America.

facts.text: The genus name Gelochelidon combines the Ancient Greek for "to laugh" with the word for swallow.
facts.quote: The genus name combines the Ancient Greek gelaō meaning "to laugh" with khelidōn meaning "swallow".
